findings: Both captures document conditional access, standard card-present pricing at no extra cost when eligible, sales or support assessment, and the developer prerequisite of an existing Android POS app or resources to build one. Stripe handles payment and compliance with the Android or React Native Terminal SDK. Apps on Devices supports a merchant POS and Stripe Reader app on one device (POS primary at startup, Stripe Reader app primary during payment, POS primary again afterward), or a POS on another device with a consumer-facing reader app over merchant-managed TCP/IP.

Both overviews list build/test, prepare for review, submit, deploy and monitor. For direct charges the intro requires one controlling platform for the connected account. The Connect section says platforms deploy only to singly controlled connected accounts and uses controller.is_controller=true.

SmartPOS OS is AOSP-based, with no Google Play Services, notifications, home screen, or production USB/ADB/debugging. Stripe handles over-the-air updates, with an 8 GB per-app device storage ceiling. Manifest permissions are automatically granted at installation with no runtime prompt, and applications requesting permissions outside the allowlist are rejected. Camera, Bluetooth and location remain experimental, with Apps on Devices NFC described as payments-only.
substantive_changes: November adds an upload private preview up to 300 MB with an email access request that does not immediately enable access. Standard Stripe API uploads still have the 200 MB limit.

November makes DevKit use an explicit development and testing prerequisite, adds a five-DevKit-per-user order limit and directs production-reader-only users to server-driven payments or standalone mode on a supported reader. May mentioned that a DevKit could be used without this explicit wording.

November adds the T600 as a compatible-reader spec route and supplies T600-specific no-main-battery/partial-write handling and T-bridge power/data requirements. Each T600 DevKit includes a T-bridge. The November Android manifest allowlist adds CHANGE_WIFI_MULTICAST_STATE while retaining the same approval and experimental behavior.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Keep May 1 as the date of the full earlier capture despite the raw filename's 2025 suffix. Preserve its S700/S710 CPU, RAM, storage, OS, pixel and density table as dated hardware evidence or a locator. November links to device-specific references instead of repeating that table.

May's lifecycle deploy step links to the Deploy API. November links instead to Dashboard deployment. Preserve the distinct API private-preview route as documented by the related deployment source. The overview link change does not establish API retirement.
conflicts: The mapped source and both Terminal concept routes cite 200 MB as an unqualified ceiling. Keep it as the ordinary Stripe API limit and identify the distinct 300 MB preview and its access condition.

The mapped source and Apps on Devices concept present the lifecycle deploy phase as API-only. November changes the overview navigation to the Dashboard, while the distinct API private-preview route has its own authorization. Dashboard and API remain distinct documented routes.

The Apps on Devices NFC warning is scoped to that platform and should coexist with the separate Terminal Collect Data private-preview route, which has its own documentation, supported devices and integration requirements. An Android manifest permission is not proof that app functionality is supported.
unresolved_questions: The pins establish that the November registration form requests early access. They give no immediate activation, approval timeline or account-specific preview entitlement.

findings: Update APK upload limit scope, DevKit and T600 hardware requirements, and the Dashboard deployment route. Keep both dated raws and the existing reciprocal Apps on Devices and Terminal concept links, adding source-side links where missing.
Scope the S700/S710 May table and retain device-specific November navigation. Keep the permissions and Connect prerequisites and add raw locators for the changed allowlist and T600 requirements.
conflicts: Correct the blanket APK limit and deploy-through-API framing in the mapped summary and the related concepts. Keep the non-payment NFC preview as a distinct Terminal route.
source_assessments.reason: A developer using the mapped overview for upload limit, deployment path, DevKit setup or T600 would miss the preview qualification and operational prerequisites.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/terminal/features/apps-on-devices/overview, source-stripe-terminal-apps-on-devices covers two Android POS architectures and needs updated developer limits and prerequisites. The merchant needs an existing Android POS app or resources to build one and requests eligibility through sales or support. Standard card-present pricing carries no extra Apps on Devices cost for eligible users. Stripe handles payments and compliance with the Android or React Native Terminal SDK. One device boots into the merchant POS app, switches the primary app to Stripe Reader during the transaction, and returns primary control to the POS after it finishes. A separate-device POS communicates over merchant-managed TCP/IP with the consumer-facing Android app on the smart reader (old raw lines 8-22, old raw lines 33-42, new raw lines 9-23, new raw lines 34-43). The developer builds/tests on a DevKit, prepares for review, submits, deploys to selected readers and monitors. The standard Stripe API APK upload max remains 200 MB, and November documents a separate private preview for up to 300 MB where the request form does not activate access immediately. November adds a five-DevKit order limit per user and T600 no-main-battery/partial-write and T-bridge requirements (old raw lines 49-69, old raw lines 71-83, new raw lines 50-76, new raw lines 80-100). The OS grants allowed manifest permissions at install without runtime prompts and rejects over-allowlist apps, with camera, Bluetooth and location experimental. Direct charges require one controlling platform, and the deploy eligibility section preserves the single-platform controller.is_controller=true qualification (old raw lines 81-87, old raw lines 128-134, new raw lines 98-105, new raw lines 146-152).
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/terminal/features/apps-on-devices/overview, source-stripe-terminal-apps-on-devices has substantive documentation updates after May 1. November 7 retains the ordinary 200 MB Stripe API cap, adds a 300 MB private preview with an email request and no immediate enablement, and makes the DevKit requirement explicit. Preserve its per-user cap, production-reader server-driven or supported standalone alternatives, and the T600's partial-write risk without a main battery and included T-bridge for DevKit power/data. The November allowlist also newly includes CHANGE_WIFI_MULTICAST_STATE, without claiming tested capability from permission alone (old raw lines 49-51, old raw lines 73-83, old raw lines 87-102, new raw lines 50-64, new raw lines 80-100, new raw lines 104-120). The two integration diagrams and numbered lifecycle formatting changed presentation. The deploy step now links to Dashboard, without changing the lifecycle phase or proving API retirement. Preserve the separately documented API private-preview route. The May inline S700/S710 specs remain dated evidence. November routes specifications to T600, S700/S710 and Verifone device pages (old raw lines 18-22, old raw lines 33-43, old raw lines 53-65, new raw lines 19-23, new raw lines 34-44, new raw lines 66-76). Keep reciprocal stripe-terminal-apps-on-devices and stripe-terminal routes, update their unqualified APK limits and the dedicated concept's API-only lifecycle description, and keep experimental permission and Apps on Devices NFC scope separate from the distinct Terminal Collect Data NFC private-preview path (old raw lines 128-134, new raw lines 146-152).
